brief: Cembalest's post-mortem opens with a market update. ISM new orders less inventories is positive and S&P 500 earnings revisions sit at the high end of history, supported by Q2 hyperscaler cloud growth of AWS 37%, Azure 43% and Google Cloud 82% plus rising backlogs, so earnings breadth has widened beyond the 2024-2025 AI-only driver. He argues that breadth is contingent: hyperscaler capital spending and R&D went from $460 bn in 2024 to $870 bn over the last 12 months, earnings breadth has run ahead of what the ISM would predict, and an unusually high share of S&P 500 earnings comes from unrealized valuation gains on Anthropic and OpenAI. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq are up about 12% this year despite a roughly 50 basis point rise in ten year yields. Treasury's August Twist has not capped the ten year, and he lists three obstacles: growth strong versus Fed Funds, worsening deficits, and hyperscaler long duration issuance equal to 68% of new Treasury long duration borrowing. He then scores a year of calls as right, wrong or open, and closes with questions about NYC's planned building seizures.
